name: Pablo Thomas
life: “I still remember counting our plants after a storm blew two down.” Friday often includes a stop at the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, where Pablo checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I was angry about the noise until I saw the pensioners on the upper deck counting our flowerpots.
appearance: Pablo is easy to recognize by short white hair and darker eyebrows and an aquiline nose and a square chin. Usually dressed in a gray fisher's sweater with a watch on a cracked leather band, Pablo counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices when listening.
personality: Pablo gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Pablo privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To learn the upper-deck passengers' favorite plant.
family: Catherine Easton is Pablo’s younger cousin. Pablo makes room at the table. Catherine brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Summer staff*, Catherine says, “I can move to a warm coast for another season.”
connections: Sebastian Hudson. Two home decorators compare the view from an overfull bus.
